name: Grade 8 — French
subject: french
description: Futur simple, comparatives, and object pronouns

questions.question: Conjugate 'partir' (to leave) in futur simple for 'je'.
questions.explanation: Futur simple = infinitive (keep the -r) + endings (-ai, -as, -a, -ons, -ez, -ont). Partir → je partirai.

questions.question: 'Plus grand que' is an example of?
'Le plus grand' expresses?
questions.explanation: Superlative uses le/la/les + plus/moins + adjective. 'Le plus grand' = the biggest/tallest.

questions.question: {{userName}} hears: 'Je te le donnerai demain.' What does 'demain' mean?
questions.explanation: 'Demain' = tomorrow. The sentence means 'I will give it to you tomorrow.' (futur simple: donnerai)

questions.question: In 'Je l'ai vu', what does 'l'' replace?
questions.explanation: 'L'' is a direct object pronoun (le/la → l' before vowel). 'Je l'ai vu' = I saw him/her/it.

questions.question: What are 'me, te, le, la, les, lui, leur' called in French grammar?
questions.explanation: These are object pronouns. Direct objects: me, te, le, la, les. Indirect objects: me, te, lui, leur.

questions.question: {{userName}} says: 'Je viendrai si j'ai le temps.' What tense is 'viendrai'?
questions.explanation: 'Viendrai' is futur simple of 'venir' (to come). Je viendrai = I will come. Irregular stem: viend-.

questions.question: 'Le mien' means?
questions.explanation: Possessive pronouns replace noun + possessive adjective. 'Le mien' = mine (masculine). La mienne = mine (feminine).

questions.question: How do you say 'I would like to travel' in French?
questions.explanation: 'Je voudrais' (conditional of vouloir) = I would like. It is more polite than 'je veux' (I want).

questions.question: How do you express 'the tallest girl' in French?
questions.explanation: Superlative after noun: la fille la plus grande. Note: definite article (la) is repeated before 'plus'.

questions.question: 'Moins grand que' is an example of?
What mood does 'bien que' (although) require in French?
questions.explanation: Certain conjunctions (bien que, pour que, afin que, quoique) require the subjunctive (subjonctif). E.g., 'Bien qu'il soit fatigué...'
